items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: Sharky worked for us a while with Harry Shields, George Brunis, and Jake Martin.

ctx.x: I thought there was as much of that type music or that style of music played everywhere else. And it wasn't some time later that we found out that this was where the thing started from and what do we call it, the cradle of jazz. And most styles, and this style evolved from New Orleans and was carried up north by some musicians, you know. But no, I wasn't conscious of that. I just thought everybody should do it that way and everybody did it that way. You'd see a guy, and what it raised me when I first began to…

Very difficult to say, some of those guys who were, or like Bunk Johnson, for instance, was a trumpet player. He could read music. He was a good reader. And others, you see, like George Lewis could never read music.
